definition: Paired-associates learning is learning to link two items together so that one helps recall the other. In the visuo-spatial form described here, it means learning associations between visual patterns and their locations, and task performance reflects visuo-spatial learning.

reasons: The packet only supports visuo-spatial paired associates learning as a task and as a measure of visuo-spatial learning; it does not define paired-associates learning generally as learning to link two items so one helps recall the other.
The added claim that the visuo-spatial form means learning associations between visual patterns and their locations is not stated in the packet.

The final clause about task performance reflecting visuo-spatial learning is only partly supported; the packet says eventual accuracy is a measure of visuo-spatial learning during the task, but not the broader definition given here.

The packet does not define “paired-associates learning” generally as “learning to link two items together so that one helps recall the other,” nor does it provide this requested sense of the term outside the visuo-spatial task context.

The packet does not state that the visuo-spatial form specifically involves “associations between visual patterns and their locations”; it only describes “visuo-spatial paired associates learning (vsPAL)” and refers to performance/accuracy as reflecting “visuo-spatial learning,” without specifying the visual-pattern-and-location pairing.
Because the definition includes substantive details not explicitly supported by the packet, it cannot be accepted under the requirement that every substantive claim be supported.
